label: bigram "i d" at the very start of the sequence (plus weaker "i i _")
explanation: Fires only in the original phase, at t=1..2 (a few weak t=3 hits): on input d when the previous input is i and that i is at position 0 or 1 ("i d ..." or "x i d ..."). It also fires weakly at t=2 on any token after "i i". Strongest at "i i d" (max) and at "i d" at t=1 (mean ~1.5 of max 2.15); "x i d" at t=2 is weaker (~0.4-0.55 of max), and "i i X" with X != d is weak (~0.2 of max). Weak tail (~3% of mass): "i X d" at t=2. Does not fire on "i d" at t>=3, at t=0, at the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase, even when the copied sequence repeats "i d". Dev: P=1.00, R=0.87, F1=0.93, mass recall 0.96.

issues: Core claims check out on the test split. The feature never fires at the delimiter or in the copy phase (activation mass share 0 in both), and never fires at t=0 or t>=4. The predicate has 0 false positives (precision 1.0). 'i d' at t>=3 gives only 0.02 precision, so the claim that it does not fire on 'i d' at t>=3 holds.

Minor systematic miss: the explanation calls the t=3 hits 'a few weak hits', but they are the exact pattern 'x i i d', with d at t=3 after 'i i'. That pattern is 27/27 active on test (precision 1.0) at about 0.40 of max, which is the same strength as 'x i d', not weak. It is a clean extension of the 'i i' context and should be in the label and predicate. It holds about 1.3% of activation mass.

The remaining misses are the tail the explanation already admits: 'i X d' at t=2 (about 0.04-0.17 of max). As a predicate term this pattern has only 0.38 precision and 2.9% mass recall, so leaving it out is reasonable.
Adding the 'i i d'@t=3 term raises test F1 from 0.933 to 0.941 and mass recall from 0.957 to 0.971, still with precision 1.0. This is a small refinement and does not refute the label.
skeptic.revised_label: "i d" at the very start of the sequence (i at position 0 or 1), plus "i i _" at t=2 and "x i i d" at t=3

final_label: "i d" at the very start of the sequence (i at position 0 or 1), plus "i i _" at t=2 and "x i i d" at t=3
